_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Life Force (1988) (Konami), USA dump
Rung used: ADR-0239 s1's second - a published RAM selector pinned for the
run. The game has no in-game stage select reachable from power-on (there is
no options menu, no code entry and no debug screen in the retail USA ROM),
so nothing on rung 1 can reach stage 2, let alone stage 6; and nothing has
to be searched for either, because the selector byte is published. Rung 3
would be a search over input for a warp that does not exist.
The selector is $0030 and the values are 00-05, one per stage of the six.
The dump is the USA one (see _releaseComment), which matters because the
only published value tables for $0030 are USA ones.
Three game facts this profile had to measure, none of them guessable and
all of them on this checkout's dump (runs/f1418/lifeforce/probe/, which is
not versioned):
1. $0030 does warp, but the byte in RAM still reads 00 afterwards - a cheat
substitutes the value the CPU reads and never writes memory - so $0030
itself can NOT be the session's RAM check: it would read 00 whether the
warp happened or not. Measured for all six values at 30 s: six visually
distinct stages, each screenshot in runs/f1418/lifeforce/probe/.
2. The attract demo ALSO reads the pinned $0030 and reaches the pinned
stage, with $0034 (P1 Lives) = 0. The entry script therefore taps Start
once at frame 120 - without that tap the run is the demo and not a game,
and the run would be scored as a warp that a player never made.
3. $000F reads 2 x the stage index: 00, 02, 04, 06, 08 and 0A for the six
values, at 4 s, 8 s, 30 s, 60 s and 120 s, and with a blind body flying
the stage as well as with none. It is the check. It is NOT in the
published RAM map: it was found by diffing the six stages' states, and it
is a check, not a cheat, so ADR-0184 s5's 'no code is invented' does not
bite - but it does mean the check is only as good as this measurement.
$0040, the published 'Is Stage Vertical? (boolean)', is reported beside
it as corroboration and is not the check: it is binary, 0 for stages 1, 3
and 5 and 1 for 2, 4 and 6, so a failed warp from 02 to 04 would pass it.
Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.

navigation.label: stage selector
navigation.source: Published twice, and the two disagree about how much they know, which is worth recording rather than smoothing over. (a) DataCrystal, Life Force (NES)/RAM map (datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Life_Force/RAM_map) lists the byte without claiming to know its values: "0x0030  ??? (Linked to stage, music theme?)". The same map does publish "0x0023  Demo Stage Num?", "0x0034  P1 Lives", "0x0040  Is Stage Vertical? (boolean)" and "0x0070  P1 Status" whose "03 - Player control" is how this profile's entry script knows the ship answers the pad. (b) Almar's Guides, Life Force Action Replay Codes (USA) (almarsguides.com/retro/walkthroughs/nes/games/LifeForce/ActionReplay/) publishes the value table verbatim: "Stage Select:  0030:??" / "Stage Select - Stage 1/Cell Stage:  0030:00" / "Stage Select - Stage 2/Volcanic Stage:  0030:01" / "Stage Select - Stage 3/Prominence Stage:  0030:02" / "Stage Select - Stage 4/Cell Stage 2:  0030:03" / "Stage Select - Stage 5/Temple Stage:  0030:04" / "Stage Select - Stage 6/Mechanical Stage:  0030:05", with the note "Switch F/X off after loading a stage". Almar's is also the page that publishes "Infinite Lives P1: 0034:03", the lives pin this profile does NOT take (see _livesComment). Measured on this dump 2026-09-26: pinning each of the six values from power-on reaches the six stages, in order, each one recognisable on screen.

_valuesComment: Value 00, stage 1 (Cell Stage), is deliberately NOT a value of this
profile. Stage 1 is what a run with no cheat reaches, so it is the
"before" side of ADR-0239 s5's union and not a place the selector has to
take anyone: a session pinned at 00 measured against the baseline pack is
the did-not-warp row that ADR-0239 s4 defines as `new == 0`. It is instead
the selector's inertness control - `cheat=0030:00` against no cheat, same
generated script, same 120 s - recorded beside the baseline, because
pinning the selector at the value the game was going to load anyway is the
one pair where a difference can only be the pin's and not the stage's.
No value overrides `entry`: the pin chooses the stage before the game
loads one, so the path from power-on to player control is the same six
times over and `defaults.entry` is the whole of it. There is no menu to
walk and no per-stage mint, which is why this folder ships two scripts and
_releaseComment: The library dump is the USA release, which this profile needs because both
published $0030 tables above are USA tables ('Life Force Action Replay
Codes (USA)', and a map whose title says Life Force (NES)). Verified three
ways on 2026-09-26: (1) its No-Intro SHA1, the 16-byte iNES header and all,
is 351EDB1FDF4BCE3BFC56D1EECCCFDC6A21BB14F4, which is the sha1 the vendored
Force (USA)" (games[395]); (2) the ROM's PRG contains the strings LIFE and
FORCE and does not contain SALAMANDER; (3) Almar's Salamander (Japan) page
shifts six of the addresses this page publishes and has no 0030 stage
select at all, so the two releases do not merely differ in name. The
No-Intro hash is the headerless one (ADR-0003); the whole-file hash
stamps into <supportedRom> (ADR-0211) and is a different number for the
same dump, not a different dump.
_chrComment: This is a CHR RAM cartridge, not a CHR ROM one: the iNES header declares 8
PRG banks and 0 CHR banks (mapper 2, UxROM), so the CHR lives in the
console's 8 KiB of pattern RAM and the game streams it there per screen.
First, `--rom-chr` has no denominator on this ROM and reports "n/a (CHR
RAM)", so s5's second denominator does not exist and the union's drawn
keys are the whole of the measurement.
Second, and against the guess that a CHR RAM game has nothing for the
builder to enumerate: its bootstrapped packs DO carry placeholders, and a
lot of them. Measured 2026-09-26 on the A/B arms' packs, the builder
scans the PRG for tile-shaped data and writes one `<tile>` per hit with
the neutral palette and the `Y` flag - 1 568 of them for this ROM, the
same 1 568 in every pack of it - against 578 and 469 drawn rules in the
two 120 s arms. s4's 2026-09-26 amendment, which drops the placeholders,
is therefore doing exactly the work it was written for here: a count over
every rule would be 2 146 and 2 037 for the two arms, and the difference
between those two numbers would be the placeholders'.
_defaultsComment: ADR-0239 s6's budget: 120 emulated seconds, the entry played once from
power-on and the body repeated to fill the run. The body is the rosette in
stage1-run.txt: it flies right, then up, then left, then down, a fixed
quarter of the run each, so the six stages are all flown whichever way
they scroll - measured 2026-09-26, $0040 says stages 2, 4 and 6 are
vertical and 1, 3 and 5 horizontal, and one body has to serve both.
The A/B behind that choice is runs/f1418/lifeforce/probe/ab/, not
versioned: the same 120 s and the same entry against a rosette body and a
forward-only body (600 f of right, then the settle), on a horizontal stage
(00) and a vertical one (05). See _abComment below for the counts.
_abComment: The A/B behind the body, four 120 s sessions recorded 2026-09-26 in
runs/f1418/lifeforce/probe/ab/ (not versioned), scored with
scripts/nav_sweep_metrics.py's pack_seen_rule_keys - the drawn keys ADR-0239
s4 gates on, read off each arm's own pack. The rosette writes 296 keys on
stage 1 and 259 on stage 6; forward-only writes 312 on stage 1 and 259 on
stage 6, and on stage 6 the two arms' key sets are not merely the same size
but the same set (259 of 259, Jaccard 1.000, the packs differing only in
the frame counts their inferred-condition comments carry). Stage 1's two
arms share 286 of their keys (Jaccard 0.888), so the 16-key difference there
is real and not noise.
What that means is that this game force-scrolls: Life Force advances the
stage on its own and the ship moves within a bounded screen ($0350, P1 X
Position, is the DataCrystal map's "unsigned, 15 to 232"), so what changes
with the body is where the ship is, not what the stage reveals. Measured
consequence: the body is worth 16 keys of 296 on a horizontal stage and 0
on a vertical one.
The rosette was kept anyway, and the price is that measured 16 keys. It is
the only one of the two bodies that presses all four directions, and the
metric s5 uses is blind to that: forward-only's advantage is an artifact of
force-scrolling, and a profile that encodes "this game scrolls right" is
wrong about three of the six stages it sweeps even when the metric cannot
see it. The two arms also disagree about nothing on the axis that was
tested, which is why the numbers are reported here rather than argued away.
_livesComment: No lives pin, and s3's control for one is therefore not owed: s3's
condition - 'it holds only when the profile's inert control passes' - is a
condition on carrying a lives pin, and this profile carries none.
Almar's does publish one, "Infinite Lives P1: 0034:03", and $0034 is
DataCrystal's "P1 Lives"; but the game draws that counter in the HUD as
the ship icons, so the counterexample s3 was amended around on Super Mario
Bros. 3 applies here too - a pin that keeps answering while the game
decrements the counter ends the run in a state the unpinned game never
reaches, and the difference would be the pin's. It is not needed: the blind
rosette body flies 120 s of each stage and the run has three ships plus a
shield, and a session that does end on the title screen still reports its
own final state, so the failure is visible in the table rather than
silently scored.
What IS run, because s3 names it as the same test ADR-0184's amendment ran
for $0030, is the selector's own inertness: `cheat=0030:00` against no
cheat at all, the same entry and the same 120 s, comparing the two
`textures/` trees byte for byte. The unpinned half of that pair is the
stage-1 baseline ADR-0239 s5 asks for anyway. It PASSES: recorded
2026-09-26 into runs/f1418/lifeforce/before/{baseline,control}, `diff -rq`
over the two `textures/` trees exits 0 with 175 files on each side and one
identical hires.txt (sha256 f3c604f3...), and both sessions' check on $000F
reads 00. A third run of the same configuration - the A/B's stage-1 rosette
arm, 120 s, `cheat=0030:00`, a different day's machine load - wrote the same
232 445 byte hires.txt with the same sha256, so the inertness is not this
pair's replay luck. Pinning the
selector at the value the game was going to load anyway changes nothing the
pack can see, which is the whole reason s3 could allow a pin to ride at all.
_metricComment: ADR-0239 s4's `new` is drawn keys - (tileData, palette) - and it is the
gate; s4 was amended on 2026-09-26 to say so and to exclude the builder's
`defaultTile` placeholders, which on this ROM is 1 568 rules of every
pack (see _chrComment). A count over every rule would be dominated by
them and would compare the same on both sides of the union.
s5's union is reported with the one denominator this ROM has. The
per-session `unique` is reported and never gates (s4).
